entry.title: Cloud-native architecture principles
entry.summary: Understand cloud-native systems as loosely coupled, declarative, observable, resilient, automated systems rather than as applications that merely happen to run in a cloud.

entry.title: CI, CD, declarative delivery, and GitOps
entry.summary: Distinguish artifact creation from release reconciliation and explain how GitOps turns version-controlled desired state into continuously reconciled application delivery.

entry.title: Metrics, logs, traces, events, and observability
entry.summary: Use metrics, logs, traces, Kubernetes events, and end-to-end probes as complementary evidence rather than treating one monitoring tool as complete observability.

entry.title: Release strategies and application debugging
entry.summary: Distinguish rolling, blue-green, and canary release ideas and debug a failed Kubernetes release from artifact through rollout, readiness, endpoints, and user traffic.

entry.title: CNCF ecosystem, projects, standards, and community
entry.summary: Place Kubernetes within the CNCF ecosystem, recognize common project responsibilities, and distinguish open interfaces, project maturity, community governance, and the landscape catalog.

entry.title: Configuration, secrets, and persistent storage
entry.summary: Separate non-secret configuration, sensitive values, and stateful volume lifecycle while respecting identity and topology.

entry.title: Container runtime and lifecycle
entry.summary: Connect an image to the runtime-created process, writable layer, isolation settings, logs, exit status, and restart behavior.

entry.title: Container networking and storage
entry.summary: Follow interfaces, published ports, bind mounts, and volumes across the isolation boundary of a container.

entry.title: Files, users, and permissions
entry.summary: Understand Linux paths, ownership, mode bits, and why service identity is part of both reliability and security.

entry.title: Git, YAML, and declarative intent
entry.summary: Use versioned text to express desired state while respecting YAML types, schema validation, review, and reconciliation.

entry.title: HTTP requests and TLS identity
entry.summary: Trace application requests above TCP and understand the separate guarantees provided by TLS encryption and certificate identity.

entry.title: Container images, layers, and registries
entry.summary: Treat an image as immutable content plus configuration, then reason about layers, tags, digests, and supply-chain movement.

entry.title: IP addresses and subnets
entry.summary: Reason about interface addresses, prefixes, local delivery, and the route choice behind every packet.

entry.title: KCNA domain map and reasoning strategy
entry.summary: Map the current KCNA blueprint to a small set of Kubernetes and cloud-native mental models so study is driven by reasoning rather than isolated terms.

entry.title: KCNA Kubernetes Fundamentals quiz companion
entry.summary: A fast review of containers, orchestration, Kubernetes architecture, CRI, and container runtimes for use beside the KCNA fundamentals quiz.

entry.title: KCNA Kubernetes Resources quiz companion
entry.summary: A compact review of Pods, YAML objects, ReplicaSets, Deployments, rollouts, apply, imperative versus declarative management, kubectl explain, and namespaces.

entry.title: kubectl apply and live state
entry.summary: Treat kubectl apply as declarative API reconciliation, compare local intent with live state, and understand why successful configuration is only one proof layer.

entry.title: Kubernetes components and the API request path
entry.summary: Trace a Kubernetes change from kubectl through the API, control-plane reconciliation, scheduling, kubelet execution, runtime, and status feedback.

entry.title: Kubernetes API and control loops
entry.summary: Understand Kubernetes as an API-driven system where controllers continuously reconcile declared intent with observed state.

entry.title: Deployments, rollouts, and rollbacks
entry.summary: Trace how a Deployment manages ReplicaSets, why template changes create rollout revisions, and how rollout evidence differs from application health.

entry.title: Labels, selectors, and ReplicaSets
entry.summary: Connect label-based selection to ReplicaSet ownership and explain how a controller continuously repairs replica-count drift.

entry.title: Kubernetes manifests and API objects
entry.summary: Read a Kubernetes manifest as a request to the API, separate desired spec from observed status, and prove what the cluster accepted.

entry.title: Kubernetes namespaces and API scope
entry.summary: Use namespaces as namespaced API scope and organizational boundaries while avoiding the common mistake of treating a namespace as automatic security isolation.

entry.title: Kubernetes networking request path
entry.summary: Trace a request from DNS through a Service and EndpointSlice to a Pod while separating CNI connectivity, Service forwarding, ingress routing, and policy.

entry.title: Pod model, lifecycle, and ownership
entry.summary: Reason about Pods as disposable execution records with one scheduled node, shared network identity, lifecycle phases, and controller ownership.

entry.title: Kubernetes scheduling and placement constraints
entry.summary: Predict where a Pod can run by separating resource requests, node selection, affinity, taints and tolerations, topology spreading, and controller intent.

entry.title: Kubernetes identity, authorization, admission, and workload boundaries
entry.summary: Separate authentication, RBAC authorization, admission, workload identity, Secret handling, Pod security, and network segmentation into clear security boundaries.

entry.title: Kubernetes persistent storage lifecycle
entry.summary: Trace durable storage from a workload claim through StorageClass and CSI provisioning to a bound volume, mounted Pod, topology constraints, and reclaim behavior.

entry.title: Namespaces and control groups
entry.summary: See containers as ordinary processes given scoped views and enforceable resource boundaries by the Linux kernel.

entry.title: Pods and workload controllers
entry.summary: Choose the smallest Kubernetes execution unit and the controller whose identity and replacement semantics match the workload.

entry.title: Ports, sockets, and DNS
entry.summary: Connect process sockets to transport ports and use DNS as name-to-record lookup rather than magical connectivity.

entry.title: Processes and finite resources
entry.summary: Build the mental model that every service is a process competing for CPU time, memory, files, and input/output.

entry.title: Routing, NAT, and firewalls
entry.summary: Follow packet decisions through routes, address translation, and stateful policy without collapsing them into one network box.

entry.title: Scheduling, resources, and health probes
entry.summary: Relate placement to requests, runtime enforcement to limits, and traffic or restart decisions to distinct health signals.

entry.title: Services, cluster DNS, and ingress
entry.summary: Separate changing Pod endpoints from stable service discovery and north-south HTTP routing through implementing controllers.

entry.title: Shells, pipes, exit status, and signals
entry.summary: Treat the shell as a process launcher and composition tool, then reason precisely about streams, status, and shutdown.

entry.title: Troubleshoot from process to pod
entry.summary: Localize failures with an evidence ladder that moves from desired state to process, network, policy, and user-visible behavior.
